title: Conditionals & ternary
description: Branch with if/else, compress with ternary, default with || and gate with && — and know exactly which values JavaScript treats as falsy.

notes: Seven falsy values: false, 0, 0n, "", null, undefined, NaN (and -0, which === 0). Empty arrays and objects are truthy.
|| returns the first TRUTHY operand; && returns the first FALSY (or last operand if all truthy). They short-circuit.
For "is this null or undefined" specifically, prefer ?? over || — otherwise 0 or "" trigger the fallback.

questions.explain: Empty array and empty object are both truthy.
&& returns the first falsy operand, or the LAST when all are truthy.

options: An expression that returns a or b
An expression that always evaluates BOTH a and b before picking one
Sugar for `cond && a || b` with identical semantics

exercises.prompt: Chain a ternary to grade a score: 90+ is A, 80+ is B, else C.
Fall back to a default with ||, then gate a value with &&.

L3.prompt: Write `classify(n)` that returns "pos" if n > 0, "neg" if n < 0, "zero" otherwise. Log classify(5), classify(-3), classify(0) on one line.
hints: Or compress with a chained ternary.
